code.title: Positive, Negative or Zero
code.description:
A reception desk program must classify any integer amount typed by the clerk. Read one integer and report whether it is positive, negative or exactly zero.

Input Format:
One line with one integer N.

Output Format:
Print Positive when N > 0.
Print Negative when N < 0.
Otherwise print Zero.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= N <= 1000000

code.title: Larger Integer with if-else
code.description:
A teacher compares two quiz scores to find the better one. Read two integers and print the larger value. If both are equal, print only the word Equal instead.

Input Format:
One line with two integers A and B.

Output Format:
Larger: <greater of A and B>
If A and B are equal, print only the single line Equal.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= A, B <= 1000000

code.title: Pass or Fail Verdict
code.description:
An online exam portal publishes results instantly. Read the marks of a student (integer out of 100) and print Pass when the marks are 40 or more, otherwise print Fail.

Input Format:
One line with one integer M.

Output Format:
Mark: <M>
Result: Pass (when M >= 40) or Result: Fail (when M < 40)

Constraints:
0 <= M <= 100

code.title: Vowel or Consonant Test
code.description:
A phonics app listens to single letters typed by children. Read one lowercase letter and print whether it is a vowel or a consonant. The vowels are a, e, i, o, u; every other lowercase letter is a consonant.

Input Format:
One line with one lowercase character C.

Output Format:
Letter: <C>
Type: Vowel (for a e i o u) or Type: Consonant

Constraints:
C is a lowercase letter from a to z.
code.inputconstrains: C is a lowercase letter from a to z

code.title: Age Group Classifier
code.description:
A vaccination drive sorts visitors into age groups. Read the age (integer) and print the group using an else-if ladder: below 13 Child, 13 to 19 Teen, 20 to 59 Adult, 60 and above Senior.

Input Format:
One line with one integer A.

Output Format:
Age: <A>
Group: Child (A < 13), Teen (13 to 19), Adult (20 to 59), Senior (60 and above)

Constraints:
1 <= A <= 120

code.title: Even or Odd Check
code.description:
A number game asks players to classify numbers. Read one integer and print Even when it is divisible by 2, otherwise print Odd. Remember that negative numbers and zero follow the same rule.

Input Format:
One line with one integer N.

Output Format:
Number: <N>
Even (when N % 2 == 0) or Odd

Constraints:
-1000000 <= N <= 1000000

code.title: Parking Fee Zone
code.description:
A mall parking gate charges a flat entry fee of 50 rupees that covers the first 2 hours. Every extra hour beyond 2 hours costs 20 rupees more (hours are always given as a whole number). Read the hours parked and print the fee.

Input Format:
One line with one integer H (hours parked).

Output Format:
Hours: <H>
Fee: <50 when H <= 2, otherwise 50 + (H - 2) * 20>

Constraints:
0 <= H <= 24

code.title: Library Late Return Category
code.description:
A college library sorts returned books into handling categories. Read the number of days a book was returned late (0 means on time) and print the category: 0 days On time; 1 to 7 days Grace period; 8 to 30 days Late; more than 30 days Defaulted.

Input Format:
One line with one integer D (days late).

Output Format:
Days late: <D>
Category: On time | Grace period | Late | Defaulted

Constraints:
0 <= D <= 365

code.title: Parcel Shipping Class
code.description:
A courier counter stamps every parcel with a handling class based on its weight in kilograms. Read the weight (integer kg) and print the class: up to 1 kg Light; 2 to 5 kg Medium; 6 to 20 kg Heavy; above 20 kg Freight.

Input Format:
One line with one integer W (weight in kg).

Output Format:
Weight: <W> kg
Class: Light | Medium | Heavy | Freight

Constraints:
1 <= W <= 50

code.title: Temperature Band Classifier
code.description:
A weather station labels each reading with a comfort band. Read the temperature in whole degrees Celsius and print the band using an else-if ladder: below 0 Freezing; 0 to 15 Cold; 16 to 30 Pleasant; 31 to 40 Hot; above 40 Extreme.

Input Format:
One line with one integer T (Celsius).

Output Format:
Celsius: <T>
Band: Freezing | Cold | Pleasant | Hot | Extreme

Constraints:
-50 <= T <= 55

code.title: Mobile Plan Selector
code.description:
A telecom shop sells four prepaid plans chosen by a numeric plan code. Read the code and use a switch statement with break in every case to print the plan name and monthly rent: code 1 Basic 199; code 2 Value 299; code 3 Max 399; code 4 Ultra 599. Any other code must print the plan name Invalid with rent 0 (handled by the default case).

Input Format:
One line with one integer C (plan code).

Output Format:
Plan: <Basic | Value | Max | Ultra | Invalid>
Monthly rent: <199 | 299 | 399 | 599 | 0>

Constraints:
1 <= C <= 99

code.title: Grade Ladder with Modifiers
code.description:
A university examiner converts marks into a letter grade with plus and minus modifiers. First pick the base grade with an else-if ladder: 90 or more A; 80 to 89 B; 70 to 79 C; 60 to 69 D; below 60 F. Then, for every base grade except F, add a modifier from the last digit of the marks: digit 7, 8 or 9 appends +; digit 0, 1 or 2 appends -; any other digit leaves the grade unchanged. A perfect score of 100 always stays plain A.

Input Format:
One line with one integer M (marks).

Output Format:
Marks: <M>
Grade: <base grade with optional + or - modifier>

Constraints:
0 <= M <= 100

code.title: Blood Donation Eligibility Desk
code.description:
A blood bank kiosk screens walk-in donors with three gates applied in order: age first, then weight, then gap since the last donation. Read the age, the weight in kg and the number of days since the last donation. A donor is eligible only when age is between 18 and 65 (inclusive), weight is at least 50 kg and the last donation was 90 or more days ago. Use nested if statements so the first failed gate decides the rejection reason: under age, over age, under weight or recent donation.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: age, weight, days since last donation.

Output Format:
Age: <age>
Weight: <weight>
Last donation: <days> days ago
Status: Eligible (all gates pass) or Status: Rejected - under age | over age | under weight | recent donation

Constraints:
1 <= age <= 100, 1 <= weight <= 200, 0 <= days <= 2000

Age: 16

code.title: Customer Tier Discount Counter
code.description:
A retail counter applies discounts by loyalty tier. Read the tier code (a single character: S Silver, G Gold, P Platinum, D Diamond) and the bill amount (a double). Discount percentage: Silver 5, Gold 10, Platinum 15, Diamond 20. Use a switch on the tier character with break in every case; any other character is Unknown with 0 discount. Print the tier name, the amount, the discount and the payable amount, with every money value shown at two decimals.

Input Format:
One line with a character T and a double A separated by a space: tier code and bill amount.

Output Format:
Tier: <Silver | Gold | Platinum | Diamond | Unknown>
Amount: <A with 2 decimals>
Discount: <discount with 2 decimals>
Payable: <amount - discount with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0 <= amount <= 1000000

code.title: Courier Cost by Weight and Zone
code.description:
A courier desk prices a parcel from its weight bracket and delivery zone. Read the weight (integer kg) and the zone code (1, 2 or 3). Base charge: up to 2 kg 80 rupees; 3 to 5 kg 150 rupees; above 5 kg 300 rupees. Zone surcharge added to the base: zone 1 adds 0, zone 2 adds 50, zone 3 adds 120. If the zone code is not 1, 2 or 3, print only the line Invalid zone. Use nested if statements: pick the weight bracket first, then decide the zone surcharge inside it.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: weight in kg and zone code.

Output Format:
Weight: <W>
Base charge: <base>
Zone surcharge: <surcharge>
Total: <base + surcharge>
When the zone code is invalid, print only: Invalid zone

Constraints:
1 <= weight <= 50, 1 <= zone <= 9
code.output1:
Weight: 2
Base charge: 80
Zone surcharge: 0
Total: 80
code.output2:
Weight: 3
Base charge: 150
Zone surcharge: 120
Total: 270
code.sampleoutput1:
Weight: 3
Base charge: 150
Zone surcharge: 50
Total: 200
code.sampleoutput2:
Weight: 10
Base charge: 300
Zone surcharge: 120
Total: 420

code.title: Menu Driven Calculator
code.description:
A classroom calculator app reads two numbers and an operator character and performs the chosen operation through a switch statement. Read two doubles A and B and an operator character op (+, -, *, /). Each case must end with break: + prints A + B, - prints A - B, * prints A * B, and / prints A / B, all results with two decimals. When op is / and B is exactly 0, print Error: division by zero instead of a result. Any other operator character prints Invalid operator.

Input Format:
One line with two doubles and a character separated by spaces: A, B, op.

Output Format:
Result: <value with 2 decimals>
When dividing by zero, print only: Error: division by zero
For an unknown operator, print only: Invalid operator

Constraints:
-1000000 <= A, B <= 1000000, op is a single character
code.inputconstrains: -1000000 <= A, B <= 1000000, op is a single character

code.title: Insurance Premium Calculator
code.description:
An insurer quotes a yearly vehicle premium from three facts: the driver age, the zone code and the no-claim years. The base premium is 5000 rupees.
- Age factor: below 25 multiplies by 1.50; 25 to 60 (inclusive) multiplies by 1.00; above 60 multiplies by 1.30.
- Zone load: zone 1 adds 0 percent, zone 2 adds 10 percent, zone 3 adds 25 percent on the age-adjusted premium. Any other zone code must print only the line Invalid zone.
- No-claim discount: 5 or more years cuts 15 percent; 3 to 4 years cuts 10 percent; 1 to 2 years cuts 5 percent; 0 years cuts nothing.
Compute the age-adjusted premium, apply the zone load, then apply the discount, and print the full breakdown with money and factor values at two decimals.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: age, zone code, no-claim years.

Output Format:
Base premium: 5000.00
Age factor: <1.50 | 1.00 | 1.30>
Zone load: <0 | 10 | 25>%
Premium after zone: <value with 2 decimals>
No claim discount: <0 | 5 | 10 | 15>%
Final premium: <value with 2 decimals>
When the zone code is invalid, print only: Invalid zone

Constraints:
18 <= age <= 90, 1 <= zone <= 9, 0 <= no-claim years <= 20

Zone load: 25%

No claim discount: 15%
Final premium: 6906.25

Base premium: 5000.00
Age factor: 1.50
Zone load: 10%
Premium after zone: 8250.00
No claim discount: 15%
Final premium: 7012.50

code.title: Traffic Fine Engine
code.description:
A traffic police console computes a speeding fine from four facts: the recorded speed, the speed limit, the vehicle class (C car, B bike, T truck) and a repeat-offender flag (Y or N). Let over = speed - limit.
- Base fine ladder on over: 1 to 10 kmh over 300; 11 to 25 over 800; 26 to 50 over 1500; more than 50 over 2500. When over is 0 or less there is no fine (base 0) and the multiplier stays 1.00.
- Vehicle multiplier applied to the base fine: car 1.00, bike 1.20, truck 1.50.
- A repeat offender (Y) pays 50 percent extra on the multiplied fine.
- The licence is suspended when over is more than 50, or when the driver is a repeat offender and over is more than 25.
Print the complete breakdown; money values with two decimals.

Input Format:
One line with two integers and two characters separated by spaces: speed, limit, vehicle class, repeat flag.

Output Format:
Speed: <speed>
Limit: <limit>
Over by: <over>
Base fine: <base with 2 decimals>
Class multiplier: <1.00 | 1.20 | 1.50>
Repeat offender: <Y or N>
Total fine: <total with 2 decimals>
License suspended: <yes or no>

Constraints:
0 <= speed <= 300, 40 <= limit <= 120, class is C, B or T, flag is Y or N

code.title: University Admission Scorer
code.description:
An admission portal filters entrance scores per department. Read the department code (1 CSE, 2 ECE, 3 MECH, 4 CIVIL) and the entrance marks (0 to 200). Use a switch on the department code with break in every case to pick the cutoff: CSE 150, ECE 130, MECH 110, CIVIL 95. An unknown code prints only the line Invalid department. Then classify the marks: marks at or above the cutoff are Admitted; marks in the 10-mark band just below the cutoff (cutoff - 10 up to cutoff - 1) are Waitlist; anything lower is Rejected.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: department code and entrance marks.

Output Format:
Department: <CSE | ECE | MECH | CIVIL>
Cutoff: <cutoff>
Marks: <marks>
Result: Admitted | Waitlist | Rejected
When the department code is unknown, print only: Invalid department

Constraints:
1 <= department code <= 9, 0 <= marks <= 200
code.output1:
Department: CSE
Cutoff: 150
Marks: 150
Result: Admitted
code.output2:
Department: MECH
Cutoff: 110
Marks: 95
Result: Rejected

Department: CSE
Cutoff: 150
Marks: 155
Result: Admitted

Department: ECE

Marks: 128

code.title: Payroll Overtime Classifier
code.description:
A payroll batch job prices overtime from the day type, the hours worked and the employee grade. Read the day code (1 weekday, 2 weekend, 3 holiday), the hours worked and the grade (A, B or C).
- An unknown day code prints only the line Invalid day code; an unknown grade prints only the line Invalid grade (the day code is checked first).
- Overtime hours: hours beyond 8 count as overtime (hours - 8 when hours > 8, otherwise 0).
- Holiday rule: when at least one hour is worked on a holiday, overtime hours are credited with a minimum of 4 (use hours - 8 when that value exceeds 4).
- Weekday hourly overtime rates: grade A 300, grade B 250, grade C 200. Weekend pays 1.5 times the weekday rate; holiday pays 2 times.
Print the breakdown with rate and pay at two decimals.

Input Format:
One line with two integers and a character separated by spaces: day code, hours worked, grade.

Output Format:
Day type: Weekday | Weekend | Holiday
Hours worked: <hours>
Overtime hours: <overtime hours>
Rate per hour: <rate with 2 decimals>
Overtime pay: <overtime hours * rate with 2 decimals>
For an unknown day code print only: Invalid day code
For an unknown grade print only: Invalid grade

Constraints:
1 <= day code <= 9, 0 <= hours <= 16, grade is a single character

mcqs.title: When Switch Beats the Ladder
mcqs.description: A switch statement is usually preferred over a long else-if ladder when:
mcqs.Option1: the condition involves ranges like marks >= 80
mcqs.Option2: several different variables must be tested together
mcqs.Option3: one single integral or character variable is compared against many constant values
mcqs.Option4: a block of code must be repeated many times

mcqs.title: Effect of break in switch
mcqs.description: Inside a switch statement, what does break do?
mcqs.Option1: It exits the switch immediately and prevents fallthrough into the next case
mcqs.Option2: It skips only the current case and continues with the next case
mcqs.Option4: It restarts the switch from the first case

mcqs.title: else-if Ladder Rule
mcqs.description: In an else-if ladder with several conditions, how many branches can execute for one input?
mcqs.Option4: Exactly one: the first true condition, or the final else when nothing matches

mcqs.title: Dangling else Pairing Rule
mcqs.description: When an else appears after two nested if statements, which if does it belong to?
mcqs.Option2: The nearest preceding if that is not already paired with an else

mcqs.title: Non-zero Integer Truthiness
mcqs.description: In C++, the condition if (n) is true for:
mcqs.Option3: any non-zero value of n, including negative numbers

mcqs.title: What Nested if Means

mcqs.Option1: an if statement written inside another if or else block
mcqs.Option2: two if statements joined with the && operator
mcqs.Option3: an if statement that has no else
mcqs.Option4: an if statement that appears only inside a loop

mcqs.title: Role of default in switch
mcqs.description: What is the purpose of the default case in a switch statement?
mcqs.Option1: It is mandatory in every switch
mcqs.Option2: It always runs before all other cases
mcqs.Option4: It runs when no other case label matches the controlling value

mcqs.title: continue Inside a Loop
mcqs.description: What does the continue statement do when executed inside a loop body?
